judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph turns on several open-textured terms — "the Business" defined only as "Spanish language and bilingual print and media business", capital "in an amount that DMSA deems appropriate", and "all expenditures must be done with the concurrence of DMSA" — each of which two parties could plausibly read differently, and it says nothing about what LSB contributes beyond "not ... any cash", leaving the pre-existing Dialogo publication's status unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its mandatory annual tax distribution and pro-rata profit distribution sit awkwardly against Paragraph 4's waterfall, which subordinates the tax distribution to full repayment of DMSA's unilaterally-sized initial capital and makes any remainder discretionary with the Board; it also interacts uneasily with Paragraph 3's reference to "Dialogo" as an existing staffed business rather than the newly-formed LLC.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The one-sided structure — DMSA free to keep and originate business while LSB is bound by "diligent efforts" and a non-compete reaching anything "to the extent it relates to the Business" — plus the merely precatory "intends to use diligent efforts", gives a court plainly nameable vague terms and a contra proferentem/one-sidedness point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The freedom it gives DMSA and its principals to compete pulls against Paragraph 1's statement that the parties form the LLC "for the purpose of jointly developing" the Business and against the opening promise here to "jointly pursue the Business"; it also switches to "the Company", a term defined nowhere in Paragraph 1.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against Paragraph 1, which names the LLC "Dialogo" and says LSB contributes no cash and nothing else, this sentence is the only hint that an existing Dialogo business and its staff come into the venture, which is precisely the kind of unreconciled gap a court must construe.
